name: County Governorates
description: A county governorate, or farmandari, is an appointed territorial administration within an Iranian province. Understanding it requires separating the county governor's coordinating responsibilities from the distinct roles of councils and specialized public agencies.

seo.title: County Governorates in Iran: Appointments and Responsibilities
seo.description: Understand Iran's county governorates, their appointed governors, administrative coordination, and relationship with local councils.

content.heading: A territorial office between province and district
content.content:
A **farmandari** is a county governorate; its head is the **farmandar**, or county governor. The territory administered is a **shahrestan**, conventionally translated as county. It should not be confused with a city: the national divisions law defines a county through neighboring districts and identifies a city within it as the administrative center. Article 12 places counties beneath provinces and above districts in the administrative hierarchy. [s1][s2]

This distinction matters when reading an address or an announcement about a public project. A county administration concerns a wider territory than its central city. References to the county governor therefore do not necessarily describe an action by the city municipality. The relevant unit and the institution responsible should be identified separately. [s1]

content.heading: Appointment and administrative coordination
content.content:
Under Article 5 of the inspected administrative resolution, the provincial governor proposes the appointment or removal of a county governor, with approval and an appointment order from the interior minister. Article 7 provides for the provincial governor to designate an acting head when the office becomes vacant or its holder cannot perform the duties. These are appointments within the executive administration. [s2]

The resolution establishes a county administrative council chaired by the county governor. Its amended reporting provisions require executive units to submit periodic performance reports to the appropriate provincial or county governor. Article 24 extends the resolution's provincial responsibilities to county governors within their territory, subject to its stated exception. These provisions describe coordination and supervision; they do not themselves demonstrate the quality of services delivered. [s2]

content.heading: How appointed administration relates to councils
content.content:
Iran's Constitution also recognizes a council framework for local affairs. Article 100 connects councils with social, economic, development, health, cultural, educational, and welfare matters, leaving their detailed powers and selection arrangements to legislation. Article 103 requires government-appointed territorial officials, explicitly including county governors, to respect council decisions within the councils' lawful authority. [s3]

The useful distinction is between institutions with different legal foundations. The county governor holds an appointed executive office, while a council operates under the constitutional and statutory framework for local representation. Reading either as a complete substitute for the other obscures how the system is designed to work. Constitutional recognition of councils also cannot establish, by itself, how much influence a particular council exercises in practice. [s2][s3]

name: District Administrations
description: A bakhshdari is the administration of a bakhsh, the territorial district beneath an Iranian county. Its appointed district head operates within a framework that also includes rural districts, village administrations, and local councils.

seo.title: District Administrations in Iran: Bakhsh and Bakhshdari
seo.description: Learn where Iran's district administrations fit, how district heads are appointed, and how rural coordination differs from council authority.

content.heading: What an Iranian district contains
content.content:
The Persian term **bakhsh** means a territorial district beneath a county, or **shahrestan**. Its administration is the **bakhshdari**, headed by a **bakhshdar**. A **dehestan**, usually translated as rural district, is a different, subordinate territorial unit. Article 12 of the national divisions law establishes this hierarchy. [s1][s2]

Article 6 describes a bakhsh as neighboring rural districts encompassing settlements and potentially towns. Its criteria consider geography, population, accessibility, and social and economic connections. A bakhsh is therefore not simply an urban neighborhood. The law also recognizes geographic differences through provisions addressing remote, border, island, desert, and other sparsely populated areas. [s1]

content.heading: An appointed office with rural connections
content.content:
Article 6 of the administrative resolution specifies nomination by the county governor, approval by the provincial governor, and an appointment order from the interior minister. Its accompanying provision allows the minister's authority under that article to be delegated to provincial governors. [s2]

An official description of rural-affairs duties published by Zanjan's provincial administration illustrates the surrounding institutional network. It assigns the provincial office work on establishing village administrations in cooperation with county and district offices, communicating rural-development objectives, and supporting village administrations with equipment and interagency coordination. These are the provincial office's published responsibilities, rather than a complete national job description for every district head. [s3]

The same document links rural administration with project monitoring, review of development proposals, and identifying villages exposed to hazards such as floods. It shows why district administration needs to be understood alongside specialist provincial offices and village institutions. It does not establish whether these tasks were completed in a particular locality. [s3]

content.title: Territorial hierarchy around a district
content.content:
```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A["Central administration"] -->|"Administrative hierarchy"| B["Province: ostan"]
  B -->|"Administrative hierarchy"| C["County: shahrestan"]
  C -->|"Administrative hierarchy"| D["District: bakhsh"]
  D -->|"Administrative hierarchy"| E["Rural district: dehestan"]
```
content.summary: The arrows show territorial administrative subordination under Article 12. They do not describe council representation, funding, or appointment procedures.

content.heading: District administration and local representation
content.content:
The district head and the district council are distinct institutions. Article 103 of the Constitution expressly includes district heads among appointed officials required to respect council decisions within the councils' authority. Article 105 also places council decisions within the constraints of national law. [s4]

These provisions make the legal boundaries important: an appointment does not eliminate council powers, while a council decision must remain within its lawful scope. For a specific development project, the meaningful questions are which institution approved it, which agency implements it, and what evidence documents progress. An organizational title alone cannot answer those questions. [s3][s4]

name: Crisis Management Organizations
description: Iran's disaster-management framework combines a national coordinating organization with provincial and county structures. Its legal arrangements distinguish policy and coordination, emergency command, participating agencies, and organized volunteer support.

seo.title: Disaster Management in Iran: Provincial and County Organizations
seo.description: Explore Iran's disaster coordination structures, escalation of emergency command, volunteer arrangements, and performance-evaluation framework.

content.heading: A system of coordination and emergency command
content.content:
Iran's Disaster Management Law, adopted in 1398 Solar Hijri, establishes coordination headquarters at national, provincial, and county levels. Article 10 assigns provincial chairmanship to the provincial governor and county chairmanship to the county governor; disaster-management managers serve as their secretaries. The national organization and territorial headquarters are therefore related but distinct parts of the framework. [s1]

Article 11 specifies escalation according to territorial reach and response capacity. A county governor can declare an emergency when necessary while informing the provincial governor. Where county capacity is exceeded, provincial assumption of command depends on the procedure set out in that article. National escalation likewise requires reporting and confirmation. Tehran city has a separate provision assigning emergency declaration and command to the interior minister. [s1]

content.title: Who chairs the coordination headquarters?
content.content:
```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A["Interior minister"] -->|"Chairs"| B["National headquarters"]
  C["Provincial governor"] -->|"Chairs"| D["Provincial headquarters"]
  E["County governor"] -->|"Chairs"| F["County headquarters"]
```
content.summary: These arrows show chairmanship under Article 10, not an automatic transfer of emergency command. Article 11 separately governs escalation and includes a special rule for Tehran city.

content.heading: How volunteers and civil organizations fit
content.content:
A regulation adopted in 1402 Solar Hijri addresses participation by civil organizations, volunteers, and private businesses. It requires provincial disaster-management directorates to implement specified coordination measures across their provinces, including counties and villages. Participating executive agencies retain responsibility for the proper execution of tasks entrusted through these arrangements. [s2]

The regulation also provides for training, exercises, documentation, and accident-insurance arrangements. During declared emergencies, coordination offices may be established in affected areas when the relevant headquarters chair determines they are needed. These offices connect participating organizations with operational headquarters and the field commander, under the field commander's supervision. [s2]

The distinction is practical: willingness to help, institutional coordination, and operational command are separate matters. The regulation describes how assistance should enter the response system; its existence alone does not establish how comprehensively volunteers have been registered, trained, insured, or deployed. [s2]

content.heading: What would demonstrate preparedness?
content.content:
A cabinet resolution adopted in 1400 Solar Hijri establishes a performance-monitoring framework. Its indicators address such matters as organizational structures, progress in making buildings and equipment safer, implementation of approved plans, staff training, and the availability of required information. It also provides for annual assessment and reporting. [s3]

These are prescribed measures, not published results. A defensible comparison between provinces would require actual observations, consistent definitions, and clear reporting periods. The inspected resolution supplies no populated annual dataset from which to rank administrations or chart improving readiness. [s3]

content.heading: Recovery extends beyond the emergency
content.content:
The government-led, United Nations-supported assessment of Iran's 1398 floods illustrates a different stage: identifying damage, losses, and recovery needs after the immediate response. Its foreword describes a pilot assessment involving government specialists, provincial departments, and United Nations technical support. It frames recovery as a basis for integrated rebuilding and development. [s4]

That assessment is a historical case, rather than a current audit of every provincial organization. Read alongside the legal framework, it helps distinguish emergency coordination from the longer work of assessing needs and planning reconstruction. Neither a command chart nor a recovery plan, by itself, proves that the intended outcomes were achieved. [s1][s4]
